---

## Breaking Changes & Fixes

### 1. `ConfigureHttpMessageHandlerBuilder` removed (compile error)
**Problem:** This API was obsoleted in .NET 7 and **removed in .NET 9**.  
**Fix:** Replaced with `UseSocketsHttpHandler((handler, _) => ...)`, which is the .NET 9 recommended API and uses the default `SocketsHttpHandler` directly—no casting needed.

### 2. `ImplicitUsings` no longer inferred without explicit opt-in
**Problem:** The .NET 8 project relied on implicit usings without declaring them in the csproj.  
**Fix:** Added `<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>` and an explicit `using Microsoft.AspNetCore.HttpOverrides;` (that namespace was never part of the implicit set).

### 3. `dotnet watch` behavioral change (runtime)
**Problem:** In .NET 9, `dotnet watch` no longer automatically restarts the app on "rude edits" (edits that can't be hot-reloaded). It now prompts interactively.  
**Fix:** Use `dotnet watch --non-interactive` in CI/containers to restore the auto-restart behavior.

---

### Additional note — Trace-level header logging
In .NET 9, Kestrel changed how connection-level data is logged. If you rely on `"Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel": "Trace"` in `appsettings` to see request headers, verify that the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Transport` category still emits what you need, or switch to the `HttpLogging` middleware with `HttpLoggingFields.RequestHeaders`.
